items.title: Sunday's roundup jumped from fossils to fungus to cactus and back to fossils
items.detail: The storyboard planned the roundup as the Taung Child fossil, then the giant fungus, then the cactus drought study, then the Homo erectus fossils and the 13-million-year-old camel fossil, every link a clean pivot. It may move same-subject stories together but didn't, and nothing in code does. The review's split-subject check caught it (through the words million year and year old); this week's triage wants to quiet that check for age phrases, which would have hidden this one.
items.fix: After the storyboard order is applied, move a later roundup story up beside an earlier one whose headline shares its subject (the same matcher the split check uses), the way a repeated kicker is already moved. Local stays first. No API cost.

items.title: Riley read pull request numbers aloud in the Meta Moment
items.detail: Sunday's Meta Moment had Riley say #569 and #580. The segment is written from the week's commit subjects, and merged pull requests end in (#569)-style numbers, which the model kept and the voice read as codes.
items.fix: Strip the (#123) pull request numbers from the commit subjects before the Meta Moment prompt, and drop any #123 left in the segment's text. No API cost.

items.title: The review card shows the calendar's focus, not the one the run used
items.detail: You judged Sunday's cuts against The Living World, but the run had moved the focus to Sky & Cosmos (it matched 10 stories) and built the deep dive and cold open around it. Monday moved too, from Music & Live Performance to Visual Arts & Heritage. The run logs the move; the card never shows it.
items.fix: Write the focus the run used, and the one it moved from, into the citations and the review summary, and show it on the Episode card beside the theme. No API cost.

items.title: A focus moved onto one-keyword matches steered Monday's deep dive and was named anyway
items.detail: Monday's week focus (Music & Live Performance) matched 1 story, so the run moved to Visual Arts & Heritage, which matched 5, each on a single keyword. The deep dive was built on them: a New Orleans cruise ship crash, a Van Gogh restitution claim, an architecture roundup and the Internet Archive union, its lead at the 51st percentile on the day's charter while 11 stronger on-theme stories went unused. The cold open then named the focus because the script, written around it, used its words 26 times.
items.fix: Let a focus centre the deep dive only when its matches clear the charter floor the Cariboo bar already uses (p70); otherwise the plain theme ranking stands. Name the focus in the cold open only on a day the deep dive was centred on it. This changes what airs, so it needs your call. No API cost.
